messages:
sophie: Quick ask — customer sent back CAIQ and wants us to explicitly state shared responsibility boundaries for encryption, logging, and incident ops across Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Can someone help draft short, copy-paste answers by EOD?

mateo: I can take a pass. Main differences: Hosted = Redwood-managed keys by default, Dedicated = optional BYOK via cloud KMS, Private = customer-managed KMS/HSM. Also logging/export access differs.

alex: +1. For CAIQ we should be explicit: 
- Encryption at rest: Hosted: platform-managed (we hold root key unless BYOK setup); Dedicated: customer can BYOK or we can manage keys for the pool; Private: customer owns keys and rotates.

priya: Need to call out audit logs too: Hosted: we retain platform logs, provide filtered customer activity logs via console/API; Dedicated: logs live in our infra but we can stream to customer S3/Cloud Logging; Private: all logs in customer environment.

jordan: Legal note: any BYOK or HSM commitments for Private require an addendum around key escrow and access. Don’t promise key escrow unless legal has signed.

mateo: Proposed short CAIQ answers (drop-in):
```
Q: Who is responsible for encryption key management?
A: Hosted: Redwood manages platform keys by default; customers may opt into BYOK for customer data via our KMS integration. Dedicated: BYOK is available and recommended for regulated workloads; Redwood manages by default only if contractually agreed. Private: customer-managed KMS/HSM; Redwood does not retain plaintext keys.
```

alex: That wording looks good. Add: "We provide key rotation hooks and logging for BYOK operations."

sophie: Can we also give a short answer for incident response ownership and SLA exceptions? They specifically asked about who handles data breach notifications when infra is shared.

priya: Short answer: Redwood handles platform incidents for Hosted and Dedicated; we notify customers per contract. Private: customer is responsible for ops and notifications unless we have a managed-services agreement. For shared infra (Dedicated with pooled services) we will coordinate and provide a runbook.

jordan: Suggest adding this sentence: "Notification timelines follow the contract's incident SLA; Redwood will support forensic requests subject to data access agreements."

mateo: I'll produce a single-page CAIQ response doc with these bullets + a simple diagram. Linking a draft architecture sketch: https://rwd.in/designs/caicq-shared-resp-draft (internal).

sophie: perfect. Who can own sending this to the customer and tracking the follow-ups?

alex: I can own the tech answers and run the internal review.

priya: I’ll handle the POC-related clarifications (what we need to enable BYOK in the POC: IAM roles, KMS permissions, sample Terraform).

jordan: I’ll do legal QA and flag any addendum needs.

mateo: I’ll assemble the doc + diagram and post in the thread. ETA 5pm PT.

infra-bot: Incident CR-2026 deployed to staging (for reference): https://rwd.in/incidents/CR-2026 — no customer impact.

sophie: Awesome — thanks team. Mateo tag me when doc is ready and I’ll send to the AE. :thumbsup:

mateo: Will do. Draft in thread before 17:00 PT.

alex: FYI — for Dedicated we should call out that KMS CMKs may be rotated by Redwood on scheduled maintenance unless BYOK enabled. I’ll add a single-sentence note.

jordan: Also include a checkbox: "Is BYOK required for POC?" so AE knows next steps.

sophie: Good idea. Closing loop: owner list = mateo (doc), alex (tech QA), priyA(priya) (POC config), jordan (legal).

priya: small correction — it's priyA (cap A) :)

sophie: noted :) thanks everyone.
